Questions students ask us first

Can I study in Italy without IELTS?

Yes — several Italian universities offer routes with or without IELTS, and some let you submit the English certificate later. The University of Padua, for example, accepts the certificate up to 31 July 2027 for the September 2027 intake, so you can apply now and prepare for IELTS in parallel.

That said, a good IELTS score (6.0–6.5) strengthens both your admission and your visa file. In your free counselling session we'll tell you honestly whether your target universities need it.

Is Italy's scholarship really fully funded?

The DSU is a regional government scholarship awarded mainly on family income, not on top marks. For eligible students it covers the full tuition fee, accommodation, meals and a yearly cash grant — which is why students call it "fully funded".

You apply for it after admission and enrolment, with family income documents prepared from Pakistan. We guide that whole file. One thing to plan for: the student visa still asks you to show proof of funds (about €10,180 for a year) before you travel — the scholarship money reaches you after arrival.

How much does your counselling cost?

Your first counselling session is completely free — bring your documents and questions, and leave with a clear plan and honest chances. If you then choose to process your applications with us, every fee (ours, the university's and the visa's) is explained in writing before you commit to anything.

When should I apply for Sweden?

For the Autumn 2027 intake: submit your application on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027, and pay the SEK 900 fee and upload your documents by 1 February 2027. One fee covers up to four programmes. Results are announced on 1 April 2027.

Sweden is strict about IELTS — you need 6.5 overall with no band below 5.5. If you haven't taken it yet, book the computer-based test now; results come in 1–5 days.

What documents do I need to get started?

Just four things for your first session: your passport, your latest transcript, your degree or certificate, and a CV in English (Europass format is what Italian universities know best — we can help you build one). Everything else — motivation letters, attestations, income documents for scholarships — we prepare with you step by step.
